title: How to make a moral agent: sentimentalism and rationalism as lenses on AI
abstract: arXiv:2611.18714v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Can AI systems be moral agents? That is, can they undertake actions that can be correctly assessed as morally right or wrong? There is no settled normative criterion of moral agency that applies neatly outside paradigm human cases. Because of the difficulties with a normative account, we instead propose a research program to explore descriptive moral agency. Most basically, we ask, what are the capabilities we humans possess that underlie our moral agency? To do so, we draw on historical scholarship in philosophy and moral psychology to isolate candidate capabilities. Then we suggest refining candidate capabilities so that they are testable in the context of AI systems. Finally, we offer specific empirical recommendations to test AI systems, especially large language models (LLMs), for those refined capabilities. Our approach offers several benefits. translated_title: 如何造就道德主体：以情感主义与理性主义审视人工智能
translated_abstract: 人工智能系统能否成为道德主体？也就是说，它们能否采取那些可以被正确评价为道德上正确或错误的行为？目前尚无一个公认的、能够妥善适用于典型人类案例之外情形的道德主体规范性标准。由于规范性阐释面临诸多困难，我们转而提出一个研究计划来探索描述性的道德主体。最根本的问题是：我们人类拥有哪些能力构成了我们道德主体性的基础？为此，我们借鉴哲学与道德心理学的历史学术研究来分离出候选能力。接着，我们建议对这些候选能力进行细化，使其能够在人工智能系统的语境中加以检验。最后，我们提出了具体的实证建议，用于测试人工智能系统（尤其是大语言模型，LLMs）是否具备这些细化后的能力。我们的方法具有若干益处。首先，它或许能够揭示人工智能系统的行为是否与其保持一致，或者（原文此处截断）……
tldr: 该论文提出以描述性而非规范性路径研究AI道德主体地位，借鉴哲学与道德心理学分离出构成人类道德主体性的候选能力并加以细化，进而为大语言模型是否具备这些能力提供了可操作的实证检验方案。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes a descriptive (rather than normative) research program for AI moral agency, isolating candidate human capabilities from philosophy and moral psychology, refining them into testable forms, and offering empirical recommendations for testing whether LLMs possess these capabilities.
